subject: Breach notification obligations — proposed compromise on timelines & cooperation
messages:
From: Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: DPA — notification timelines and forensic access

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo. Our legal team sent over a DPA redline and they have flagged the incident notification and cooperation sections as negotiable items. Two points they asked us to raise: 1) a 24-hour notification requirement for any "suspected" data breach affecting PII/PHI, and 2) contractual access to forensics/metadata for investigations (they want query-level logs and sample data exports for proof of harm).

We recognize Redwood's position on stability and operational burden, but Greenfield's compliance review is strict due to regulatory oversight. Can Redwood confirm whether 24 hours is feasible, and whether we can include explicit language allowing us limited forensics access in emergencies?

I've attached our current redline (DPA_redline_v3.pdf) for reference. If it's easier, happy to schedule a quick call to go through the asks.

Best,
Tom Weaver
Head of Legal Operations
Greenfield Health

--
Attachment: DPA_redline_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 214 KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-03T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA — notification timelines and forensic access

Tom — thanks for sending and for the clear asks. Looping in Neha (legal) and Marcus (platform ops) so we can triage internally and propose a compromise. Quick notes from my side:

- 24 hours for *suspected* incidents is unusually short for multi-tenant hosted services; we typically commit to 72 hours for confirmed incidents while keeping customers updated during triage.
- Forensics access: we can provide relevant logs and scoped exports under an NDA and with clear limits, but full direct query access to our tenant servers is not something we expose.

Neha / Marcus — can you weigh in with what we can accept and suggested language? Tom — if you have strict regulator-driven language we should see that too (specific statute/regulatory citation helps).

I propose a 3-way: 72-hour notification for confirmed incidents, rolling updates within the 72-hour window, and a defined emergency cooperation process that includes: limited log exports, documented data samples, and an expedited evidence request path under NDA.

Happy to jump on a call later today.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-03T14:40:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA — notification timelines and forensic access

Thanks Rachel. Internal legal notes below (draft language suggestions included). High level: we need to limit exposure while giving Greenfield the observability they need for compliance.

1) Timeline: We will agree to "notification of confirmed security incidents affecting Customer Data within 72 hours of confirming a breach." For suspected incidents, we propose "initial acknowledgment within 24 hours" with a clear distinction that the 24-hour item is an acknowledgment of investigation status, not a completed root-cause or full notification.

Suggested clause: "Vendor shall acknowledge receipt of any Customer report of a potential security incident within 24 hours and shall provide written notification of any confirmed security incident affecting Customer Data within 72 hours of confirmation. Vendor will provide regular updates during the investigation at intervals not to exceed 48 hours."

2) Scope: Limit to incidents resulting in unauthorized access, exfiltration, or alteration of Customer Data. Exclude operational outages and non-customer-impacting maintenance.

3) Cooperation / Forensics: We can provide forensics artifacts (system logs, relevant KV cache snapshots, request traces) where available, subject to: a) a mutually-executed limited-scope NDA or Data Processing Agreement amendment, b) redaction of unrelated tenant data, and c) clear preservation of Vendor's operational security controls. We will not allow external parties to run arbitrary queries against production systems.

Suggested cooperation language: "Vendor shall reasonably cooperate with Customer and, where permissible under Vendor's operational and security policies, provide relevant forensic artifacts and summaries. Any such provision of logs or derived data shall be limited to the minimum necessary and shall exclude data belonging to other Vendor customers. If Customer requires access to data hosted on Vendor's platform beyond provided artifacts, such access must be performed by Vendor personnel or under explicit written agreement with additional safeguards."

Marcus — are the artifacts described above (logs, traces, cache snapshots) available in our standard incident toolkit? If not, what is the expected time to produce?

-Neha

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-04T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA — notification timelines and forensic access

Quick infra feasibility note: we can produce the following within the proposed timelines:
- Initial ack (24h): trivial (automated)
- Confirmed incident notification (72h): possible for most incidents; 72h gives us time to validate scope and remediate obvious containment steps.
- Artifacts: request traces and request-level logs (timestamped, request-id correlated) — generally available, but we need to scrub other tenant identifiers. Exporting a sample dataset or CSV of affected records will take longer depending on the data model; plan for 3-5 business days for curated exports.

Operational constraints to flag to the customer: we cannot provide raw disk images or run remote queries on production clusters. All forensic exports will be executed by Redwood staff in a controlled environment. We also require an expedited evidence request form and an authorized contact list before we start any export.

I'll draft a short appendix describing typical artifacts and turnaround times and share in the repo.

-Marcus

--

From: Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@greenfieldhealth.com>

Subject: Re: DPA — notification timelines and forensic access

Rachel / Neha / Marcus — thanks for the thoughtful and fast responses. Greenfield is amenable to the compromise you propose. To summarize the agreement from our side:

- Greenfield will accept the 24-hour *acknowledgment* plus 72-hour *confirmed notification* approach.
- Greenfield understands forensic artifacts will be provided under NDA and that Redwood staff will perform exports.

Two follow-ups before we finalize:
1) Can Redwood add the language that requests "regular updates not to exceed 48 hours" during investigation in the DPA? (Neha suggested text above which looks good to us.)
2) Please share the SOC 2 summary and the subprocessors list as part of the procurement packet (we need this for our compliance team).

If you can update the redline with the agreed text and push a version to the shared Drive link, our legal ops will review and sign. Happy to get this done this week.

Best,
Tom Weaver
Head of Legal Operations
Greenfield Health
